err.internal: An unexpected error occurred: {detail}. If it keeps happening, check the logs. e.g. the newest log file in {logsDir}
err.didYouMean: Unknown command: {input}. Did you mean `{suggestion}`? e.g. blert {suggestion} --help

err.usage: The input format is not valid. Usage: {usage}  e.g. {example}

err.addType: Unknown alert type: {value}. Use one of {types}. e.g. blert add change ETH 5% 1h
err.addTypeDidYouMean: Unknown alert type: {value}. Did you mean `{suggestion}`? e.g. blert add {suggestion} --help
err.mode: Unknown repeat policy `{value}`. Use one of once, cooldown:<time>, hyst:<percent>. e.g. --mode cooldown:10m
err.modeRange: The cooldown `{value}` is outside the allowed range (1 minute to 24 hours). Enter a value between 1m and 24h. e.g. --mode cooldown:30m

err.noInput: Cannot read input. Run this in a terminal that accepts input. e.g. type blert init directly in the terminal
err.invalidAnswer: The answer was not understood, so setup was stopped. Enter one of the suggested values. e.g. y or n, or a number for presets
err.initDeclined: Setup was stopped because the notice was not accepted. To accept, run it again and enter y. e.g. blert init
err.presetSub: Unknown preset subcommand: {value}. Use one of {subs}. e.g. blert preset list
err.presetSubDidYouMean: Unknown preset subcommand: {value}. Did you mean `{suggestion}`? e.g. blert preset {suggestion}
err.presetUnknown: There is no preset `{value}`. Check the names with `blert preset list` (available: {slugs}). e.g. blert preset install major-swing
err.presetUnknownDidYouMean: There is no preset `{value}`. Did you mean `{suggestion}`? e.g. blert preset install {suggestion}

help.title: blert — a CLI that delivers Binance spot and futures alerts on your own PC
help.footer: Detailed usage for each command: blert <command> --help

help.cmd.init.summary: Run the initial setup interactively (notice, sound, preset)

blert add volume SOL x4 5m/1h

blert lang ko

quiet.warn.exempt: Warnings such as liquidation proximity and lost connections still sound (add --include-warn to silence them too).
quiet.now.off: it is not quiet time now
quiet.set.done: Quiet every day {from}-{to} (this PC's local time). {scope} Right now: {now}.
quiet.off.done: The daily quiet hours are off.
quiet.off.none: No daily quiet hours are set.
quiet.status.snoozeOff: Snooze: off (turn on with blert snooze 1h)
quiet.status.scheduleOff: Daily quiet hours: off (turn on with blert quiet 23:00-07:00)
err.snoozeUsage: Give only one duration. e.g. blert snooze 1h (turn off with blert snooze off)
err.snoozeFlags: Options cannot be used to show the status or turn snooze off. e.g. blert snooze off
err.snoozeRange: The quiet duration `{value}` is outside the allowed range (1 minute to 7 days). e.g. blert snooze 4h
err.quietUsage: Give only one time range. e.g. blert quiet 23:00-07:00 (turn off with blert quiet off)
err.quietFlags: Options cannot be used to show the status or turn quiet hours off. e.g. blert quiet off
err.quietFormat: The time range `{value}` is not valid. Use HH:MM-HH:MM between 00:00 and 23:59. e.g. blert quiet 23:00-07:00
err.quietSame: The start and end are the same (`{value}`). Use two different times. e.g. blert quiet 23:00-07:00

err.soundResetUsage: Give only one slot to reset. e.g. blert sound reset up, blert sound reset all

err.soundDeclined: The '{kind}' sound was not installed. To install it, run the command again and enter y. e.g. blert sound set {kind} ./alert.wav
err.soundInvalid.too-large: The sound file is too large (it must be 512KB or less). Shorten it and try again. e.g. blert sound set up ./short.wav

err.soundInvalid.bad-format: Unsupported WAV format ({detail}). It must be mono or stereo, 16-bit, 8,000-48,000Hz. e.g. export as 'WAV (PCM 16-bit, 44100Hz)' from an audio editor

err.download.insecure: Only https URLs can be used. e.g. https://example.com/up.wav (sound) or https://example.com/preset.json (preset)
err.download.redirect: Stopped because the server tried to send you to another address ({url}). Give the https URL on the same site directly. e.g. https://example.com/up.wav
err.download.too-large: Stopped because the file is too large (limit {limit}KB). Use a smaller file. e.g. blert sound set up ./short.wav

err.themeField: The `{field}` item in the theme file is missing or not valid. It needs name, version, license, and a url and sha256 (64 characters) for each of up, down, account and warn. e.g. blert sound theme ./theme.json (name, version, license, sounds.up.url, sounds.up.sha256 …)

err.keyApiKey: The API key is empty or not in a valid format. Enter the API key string (letters and digits) that Binance issued after you registered the public key. The public key itself is not the API key. e.g. 64 letters and digits
err.keyFile: Cannot read the key file: {path}. Enter the path of the private key PEM file. e.g. C:\Users\me\blert-keys\private_key.pem
err.keyDenied: This key is not read-only, so it is not saved or used (permissions enabled: {fields}). In Binance API Management, create a key with only reading enabled and trading, withdrawal, margin and futures turned off, then register it again. e.g. a new Ed25519 key with only 'Enable Reading' on and restricted IPs
err.keyNoRead: This key has no read permission, so it cannot be used for account alerts ({fields}). Turn on reading in Binance API Management. e.g. a key with 'Enable Reading' on
err.keyRejected: Binance rejected this key ({detail}). Check that the API key and the private key belong to the same key pair and that this PC's IP is in the allowed IP list. e.g. add your current IP to the allowed IPs in Binance API Management
err.keyUnverified: Could not verify the key permissions ({detail}). Check your internet connection and PC clock, then try again. e.g. blert key check
err.keyNone: No key is saved. Register a key first. e.g. blert key add

help.cmd.start.summary: Start monitoring in the background — keeps monitoring after you close the terminal
help.cmd.start.examples:
blert start
blert start && blert status
help.cmd.stop.summary: Stop the background monitor (saves state and exits cleanly)
help.cmd.stop.examples:
blert stop
blert stop && blert status
help.cmd.status.summary: Show whether monitoring is running and its state (alert count, connections, latest gap)
help.cmd.status.examples:
blert status
blert start && blert status
help.cmd.logs.summary: Show the logs (-n number of lines, -f keep following)
help.cmd.logs.examples:
blert logs
blert logs -n 20
blert logs -f
start.ok: Started the background monitor — PID {pid}. Monitoring continues after you close the terminal. Check it with blert status, stop it with blert stop
err.startTimeout: The background monitor was not ready within {seconds}s, so it was stopped. Check the logs for the cause. e.g. blert logs -n 30
err.startExited: The background monitor exited while starting (exit code {code}). Check the logs for the cause. e.g. blert logs -n 30
stop.notRunning: No background monitor is running. To start one: blert start
stop.requested: Asked the background monitor (PID {pid}) to stop...
stop.done: Stopped the background monitor. State saved.
stop.forced: The background monitor did not respond within {seconds}s, so it was stopped by force. The last state may not have been saved. To start again: blert start
stop.crashed: The background monitor had already ended abnormally (last alive {alive}). To start again: blert start
err.stopForeground: blert monitoring is running in the foreground (blert run, PID {pid}). Stop it with Ctrl+C in that terminal. e.g. press Ctrl+C in the terminal where it runs
status.none: blert monitoring is not running. To start: blert start (to watch in this terminal: blert run)
status.starting: Starting (alert and connection status will appear when it is ready)
status.foreground: blert monitoring is running in the foreground (blert run) — PID {pid}. It is not a background monitor, so it ends when you close that terminal. To use the background monitor, stop it with Ctrl+C and run blert start
status.crashed: blert {mode}: it seems to have ended abnormally (last alive {alive}). Monitoring is stopped. To start again: blert start
warn.daemonDied: Warning: the blert background monitor seems to have ended abnormally (last alive {alive}). Monitoring is stopped. To start again: blert start
logs.none: There are no logs yet. They are written to {dir} once monitoring starts
err.logsLines: The number of lines must be an integer of 1 or more (`{value}`). e.g. blert logs -n 20
help.cmd.service.summary: Register or remove automatic start of the background monitor at login (Windows)
help.cmd.service.examples:
blert service install
blert service uninstall
service.taskDescription: Starts blert monitoring automatically at login (remove with blert service uninstall)
service.confirmHeader: The following will be registered in Windows Task Scheduler (administrator rights are not needed):
service.confirmUpdate: A task with the same name already exists and will be replaced with the new one.
service.installed: Registered automatic start. The blert background monitor will start automatically from your next login. To start it now: blert start. To remove: blert service uninstall
service.removed: Removed automatic start. A running background monitor was left as it is. To stop it: blert stop
service.absent: There is no automatic start registered.
err.serviceUnsupported: Automatic start is not supported on this operating system yet. Only Windows is supported for now. Run it yourself instead. e.g. blert start
err.serviceNpx: Automatic start cannot be registered from the temporary path used by npx (the path may disappear). Install blert globally and try again. e.g. npm install -g @eungang/blert, then blert service install
err.serviceMissingFile: The executable could not be found, so nothing was registered ({path}). Check the installation or build. e.g. npm run build
err.serviceRegister: Could not register with Task Scheduler ({detail}). Check that the Task Scheduler service is running. e.g. check directly in Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc)
err.serviceUnregister: Could not remove automatic start ({detail}). You can delete the blert task directly in Task Scheduler. e.g. delete the blert task in taskschd.msc
status.service.none: Automatic start: not registered (to register: blert service install)
status.service.broken: Automatic start: the registered path cannot be found ({path}). Register it again. e.g. blert service install
help.cmd.channel.summary: Register, remove or test an external alert channel (Telegram), and turn account alerts on or off — off by default
help.cmd.channel.examples:
blert channel add telegram
blert channel test
blert channel account off
blert channel remove
err.channelType: Telegram is the only supported external channel (`{value}`). e.g. blert channel add telegram
channel.disclosure1: The external alert channel (Telegram) is off by default and is turned on only when you register it.
channel.disclosure2: When on, alert text (price alerts, monitoring gap warnings) is delivered to your phone through Telegram's servers. The text may remain on Telegram's servers.
channel.disclosure3: Account alerts such as fills, balances and liquidation price are sent only if you allow them separately below. API keys and private keys are never sent.
channel.disclosure4: The bot token is stored only in the OS keychain and never in the settings file.
channel.askAgree: Do you agree with the above and want to continue? (y/N)
err.channelDeclined: The external channel was not registered because you did not agree. Register it again if you need it. e.g. blert channel add telegram
err.channelNoKeychain: The OS keychain cannot be used here, so the channel token is not saved. Tokens are never stored in files or environment variables instead, and desktop notifications keep working. On Linux a Secret Service (such as gnome-keyring) is required. e.g. sudo apt install gnome-keyring
channel.promptToken: Telegram bot token (the string you got from BotFather):
err.channelToken: The bot token format is not valid. Enter the string BotFather gave you, like `123456789:AAH...`. e.g. send /newbot to @BotFather in Telegram to get a token
err.channelTokenRejected: Telegram rejected this bot token. Check the token again. e.g. send /token to @BotFather in Telegram to get it again
err.channelNetwork: Could not connect to the Telegram server. Check your internet connection and try again. e.g. blert channel add telegram
channel.waitMessage: In the Telegram app, open the bot you just created and send it any message (e.g. /start). Send it in the Telegram app, not in this terminal. Waiting up to {seconds}s...
channel.noMessage: No message received by the bot was found. Check that you sent it to the same bot (the one you just got the token for). You can also enter the chat ID yourself.
channel.promptChatId: Enter the chat ID (a number; for groups it may start with -):
err.channelChatId: The chat ID must be a number (`{value}`). Send a message to the bot and try again. e.g. blert channel add telegram
channel.askAccount: Also send account alerts such as fills, balances and liquidation price to Telegram? They are not sent by default. (y/N)
channel.testMessage: This is a blert connection test. If you can see this message, the alert channel is connected.
err.channelSendFailed: Could not send the test message ({reason}). Check the token and chat ID. Nothing was saved. e.g. blert channel add telegram
channel.replaced: Replacing the existing Telegram channel settings with the new ones.
channel.addedAccountOn: Registered the Telegram channel. Price alerts, monitoring gap warnings and account alerts will be delivered to your phone (to turn account alerts off: blert channel account off). Test: blert channel test, remove: blert channel remove
channel.addedAccountOff: Registered the Telegram channel. Price alerts and monitoring gap warnings will be delivered to your phone (account alerts excluded; to turn them on: blert channel account on). Test: blert channel test, remove: blert channel remove
channel.removed: Removed the Telegram channel. Nothing is sent outside any more.
channel.none: No external channel is registered. To register one: blert channel add telegram
err.channelNone: No external channel is registered, so there is nothing to test. Register one first. e.g. blert channel add telegram
channel.testSent: Sent the test message. Check your phone.
notify.telegramFailed: Could not send the Telegram alert ({reason}). Desktop notifications are fine. Check the token, chat ID and internet connection. e.g. blert channel test
channel.chatIdInvalid: The chat ID must be a number (`{value}`). Enter it again.
err.channelNoneAccount: No external channel is registered, so the setting cannot be changed. Register one first. e.g. blert channel add telegram
channel.accountAsk: Account alerts such as fills, balances and liquidation price will be delivered to your phone through Telegram's servers. Turn them on? (y/N)
channel.accountOn: Account alerts are also sent to Telegram. To turn them off: blert channel account off
channel.accountOff: Account alerts are not sent to Telegram (public market alerts and monitoring gap warnings are still sent). To turn them on: blert channel account on
